ans_h2: What this jig is, who it is for and what it changes
ans_p: The FUJI NXT Feeder Calibration Jig from Southern Machinery is a bench-top maintenance station for FUJI NXT tape feeders. A 50X CCD camera with LED lighting looks at the feeder pick-up window, a monitor shows the image with a cross cursor, and a motor drives the feeder lever in single or continuous strikes at an adjustable speed. The technician centres a standard calibration ruler on the cross cursor once, locks the X, Y and H wheels, and then checks every feeder against that same reference, adjusting the feeder until the component centre and the cross cursor coincide. It is used for repaired feeders, used-feeder incoming inspection, scheduled maintenance and high-throw-rate troubleshooting.

why_h2: A feeder a few tenths off looks like a placement problem
why_lead: When a feeder is worn, repaired or set up by feel, the pick-up point drifts. The machine still runs, but the nozzle reaches for a part that is not quite where it should be. The line sees throws, mis-picks and stops - and the first suspects are usually the nozzle, the vision system or the program.
w1t: Throws and mis-picks with no obvious cause
w1d: A feeder that indexes short or long, or a worn lever, moves the component away from the pick-up point. The symptom shows up at the head, so the hunt starts in the wrong place.
w2d: Every feeder swapped in and out on the line costs production minutes. Without a reference, two technicians can disagree about the same feeder and both be partly right.
w3t: Repaired and used feeders arrive unverified
w3d: A feeder back from repair, or bought second-hand, has no proof that it feeds to the right position. Without a check it goes straight to the line and becomes the line's problem.
why_quote: Keep feeder problems in the maintenance room, not on the SMT line.

how_lead: Each function below is taken from the Southern Machinery user manual for this jig. The diagram underneath is a concept view of the workflow, not a drawing of the machine.
h1d: A high-magnification CCD camera with LED lighting looks into the pick-up window, so the component position, the thimble movement and lever wear are visible on the monitor.
h2d: A motor operates the feeder lever like the machine does - one strike per press, or continuous - with a speed control, so you can watch the feed step by step or at speed.
h3t: X, Y and H wheel gears

h4d: A calibration ruler fitted in a reference feeder defines where the component centre should be. Every feeder is then judged against that one reference, not against an opinion.

learn_h2: A 30-minute study route for the technician who will own the jig
learn_lead: Adapted from Southern Machinery's learn-SMT-in-3-hours training method: one question per block, a completion check at the end of each, and every value tied to the user manual or marked To be confirmed. This is a learning aid, not a replacement for the manual or your site safety procedure.
l1t: 0 - 5 min: Where the feeder sits in the line
l1d: The feeder presents the part; the head picks it at a fixed point. If the part is not at that point, the head, the camera and the program all look guilty.
l1c: Check: explain why a feeder fault shows up as a pick-up error.
l2d: CCD image of the pick-up window, cross cursor, thimble up-and-down movement, lever wear and tape-guide cover condition.
l2c: Check: name three things you can see on the monitor.
l3d: Fit the calibration ruler in a reference feeder, focus with H, centre with X and Y, then lock. After this, X, Y and H are not touched again.
l3c: Check: say which wheel you turn first and why.
l4d: Mount the feeder with the ruler, press Auto/Manual, compare the component centre with the cross cursor, adjust the feeder bolt-pin until they coincide, check the wheel gear, lock the screws.
l4c: Check: complete one feeder under supervision.
l5d: Write down feeder ID, date, what you saw, what you adjusted and the recheck result. Clean the jig and protect the ruler.
fc_lead: Start with a safe state and stop at the first point you are not authorised for.
fc1: Observed symptom: write down the feeder ID, slot, part number and alarm text as seen.
fc2: Safe state: take the feeder off the machine following your site procedure.
fc3: Reference: confirm the jig still shows the calibration ruler centred on the cross cursor.
fc4: First check: strike the lever on the jig and compare the component centre with the cross cursor.
fc5: Confirmed and authorised: adjust, lock, recheck, record. Not confirmed: tag the feeder and escalate.
mc1: Evidence: Verified source - user manual, maintenance and service
mc2: Keep the jig clean and do not knock the jig body while testing.
mc3: After use, clean it and apply a little AFC grease to the feeder fixing seat.
mc4: Keep the calibration ruler intact; a bent ruler moves the reference.
mc5: Monitor dark at power-on: check the power connection, then the signal wire.
mc6: Maintenance interval: To be confirmed for your workload.

faq_h2: Questions buyers ask before they order
q1: Which feeders does this calibration jig work with?
a1: The Southern Machinery user manual states that the jig is for FUJI NXT feeders. Feeder widths and any other platform are confirmed per order. Send a photo of the feeder nameplate and we will confirm the fit.
q2: What exactly does the jig check?
a2: It shows the feeder pick-up window at 50X with LED lighting on a monitor with a cross cursor. You can see whether the component centre sits on the cross, how the thimble moves up and down, lever wear and the tape-guide cover condition.
q3: How is a feeder corrected on the jig?
a3: After a one-time setup with the calibration ruler, you mount the feeder, press Auto/Manual and compare the component centre with the cross cursor. If they do not coincide, adjust the feeder bolt-pin until they do, check the wheel gear and lock the screws.
a4: The user manual describes a motor-driven lever strike. One product image and an older quotation mention pneumatic drive and 5 kg/cm2 air pressure. Ask us to confirm the drive of the build you order before you plan the bench.
q5: What power supply does it need?
a5: The user manual states 220 V AC, 50 Hz, 60 W. A how-to presentation states 110 / 220 V AC, 50 / 60 Hz. Tell us your mains supply and we confirm the power option on the quotation.
a6: The user manual lists the machine unit, an LCD monitor and the user manual; the calibration ruler is part of the calibration procedure. The current standard package is confirmed on your quotation.
q7: What does it cost and how long is delivery?
a7: Price, lead time, warranty and payment terms are quoted for the configuration you need and are not published on this page. Send your feeder model, quantity and destination for a quotation.
q8: Is Southern Machinery affiliated with FUJI?
a8: No. Southern Machinery is an independent Shenzhen manufacturer. FUJI and NXT are used here only to describe the feeders the jig is built to check.
